title: micro-mentor-currency-and-onboard-access-playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for trialing a low-friction, credit-based mentor program paired to a lightweight onboarding access checklist. Goal: reduce first-21-day friction for new hires while distributing mentor load more fairly across ICs and managers. Treat as experiment; feedback loop after each cohort.

Overview / problem statement:
- New hires often bottleneck on 3 things: 1) access to systems, 2) tribal product/infra knowledge, 3) contextual onboarding tasks (who to ping, where to find runbooks).
- People Ops currently coordinates access but we rely heavily on a small cohort of volunteer mentors. That leads to burnout and uneven new-hire experiences.
- Proposal: micro-mentor currency (MMC) + compact access checklist that any mentor/buddy can honor in ~30–60 minutes/day for first 14 days. Mentor activity is tracked as "currency" and can be redeemed for time off credits, retroactive availability, or recognition at performance calibration.

Experiment scope:
- Roles: SWE (backend), SWE (infra), SRE, Product, Solutions Eng. Start with 6 hires in Sept 2025 cohort.
- Mentor pool: opt-in engineers across Platform, SRE, and Product (target 18 participants so each mentor supports ~1–2 hires).
- Duration: 21 days per hire (day 0 = offer accepted -> first 21 working days).
- Success metrics: time-to-first-successful-deploy (target <= 10 days for backend hires), number of access-related blockers per hire (target <= 2 in first 7 days), NPS from new hire onboarding survey (target >= 8/10).

Micro-Mentor Currency (MMC) model:
- Earn rules: mentors log discrete interactions (40–60 min pair session = 3 MMC; 15–20 min quick unblock = 1 MMC; landing-page review or code walkthrough = 2 MMC).
- Redemption options (quarterly): 1 MMC = 30 minutes mentor credit applied to mentor's backlog; 10 MMC = 1 day flexible time-off credit; manager-approved special recognition for high earners.
- Tracking: simple shared Google Sheet for MVP + Slack #mmc log channel where mentors post quick tags (e.g., "+MMC 2 @mentor-name hire-anna" with link to onboarding sheet).
- Governance: People Ops reconciles MMC every 30 days and publishes small badge on internal profile; managers confirm redemptions.

Compact Access Checklist (MVP) — to be completed by day 3 by People Ops + assigned mentor/buddy:
- Pre-day-0 (recruiter/people ops): device shipped, GitHub account invited, company email created, Okta invite, VPN/VPC access request started, calendar invites for first-week ramp set.
- Day 0 (IT + people ops): laptop received & imaged, first login to email, sign in to Okta, slack join #team, add to relevant Google Groups, verify MFA set up.
- Day 1 (mentor): code repo access confirmed, CI pipeline read-only access, access to dev/stage environment credentials (secrets manager view), run the sample local dev environment (step-by-step mini-runbook executed together), first tiny PR merged from tutorial template.
- Day 3 (mentor): verify monitoring/dashboard access (Grafana/Datadog), pager rotation stub added with read-only view, SSO to console validated, deployable micro-change path success (deploy to dev or feature branch).

Interview rubric additions (for mentor-aligned hiring):
- Quick rubric for screening mentors/buddies (opt-in): available time/week (0–5 scale), prior onboarding experience (0/1 binary), domain familiarity with role (0–3), willingness to log MMC (0/1). Use this to prioritize mentor assignments.

Candidate-facing hiring plan snippet (for hiring managers):
- Sourcing: emphasize role growth as mentor pairing opportunity; list mentoring expectation in JD ("first 3 months paired with a rotational mentor for onboarding").
- Interview loop (MVP): 1) Hiring manager screen (behavioral + outcomes), 2) Technical take-home (small task with 4–6 hour ask), 3) Pairing session (30–45 min: collaborative problem + emphasis on communication), 4) Team fit (culture + mentorship questions).
- Rubric highlights (scoring 1–4): clarity of thought, problem decomposition, product tradeoffs, communication with non-technical partners, expected ramp speed. Calibrate to role seniority: IC2 vs IC3 thresholds.

Onboarding week-by-week checkpoints (template to copy into hire's onboarding doc):
- Week 0 (preboarding): welcome doc + maps, hardware, calendar, intro to MMC and assigned buddy, invite to cohort intro call.
- Week 1: local dev runbook, first PR, meet product partner, complete security training, verify all access items.
- Week 2: small ship goal (feature or infra change) + postmortem template, 1:1 with mentor to review blockers and MMC balance.
- Week 3: demo to team, plan 30/60/90 draft, survey about experience and NPS.

Mentor quick playbook (for day-to-day):
- Day 0–3: prioritize access & dev environment; aim for at least one completed local run.
- Daily: 15–30 min quick sync or async review; if blocked escalate to SRE/platform channel.
- Week 1: pair on first PR, review PR template; leave prioritized next-step for hire.
- Week 2: help hire own a small ship; guide through rollout checklist and infra runbook.

Operational notes (implementation details):
- Tools: temporary Google Sheet + Slack logs for MVP. If adopted -> integrate with people-ops portal and an internal reward ledger (work with Finance to design redemption workflows).
- Compliance: any time-off redemption must be approved by manager; MMC logs are visible to managers for calibration.
- Data retention: MMC logs kept for 1 year. Onboarding survey responses stored in People Ops Qualtrics folder.

Open questions / known risks:
- Will mentors reliably log MMC without friction? (mitigation: Slack shortcut + quick form)
- Equity: will high-visibility mentors profit more? Need rotation safeguards.
- Finance: how to budget for MMC redemptions that translate to time-off replacements?
- Does MMC create perverse incentives (mentors prioritizing quick tasks to earn currency)?

Next steps / action items (owner tags):
- Build MVP sheet + Slack channel (#mmc) — owner: Priya Kapoor — due 2025-08-18.
- Recruit volunteer mentors + run short orientation (30 min) — owner: Marcus Chen — due 2025-08-25.
- Draft People Ops policy for redemption & visibility — owner: Sofia Martinez — due 2025-09-05.
- Sync with Finance about redemption accounting — owner: Liam O'Neal — due 2025-09-10.

Quick templates to copy into hire doc (copy/paste):
- "MMC log entry" example: +MMC 3 @sofia hire-jamie why: paired on dev-runbook PR#12 link:https://github.com/example/repo/pull/12
- "First-PR checklist" snippet: set up branch -> run tests locally -> create draft PR -> add reviewer -> deploy to feature branch -> confirm metrics updated -> merge.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this lean. We want to lower friction, not add bureaucracy. If mentors say logging is a pain, pivot to weekly digest model where mentors email a short list and People Ops credits MMC centrally.
- Watch for mentors gaming system; small audit sample each month (random hire-mentor pair review).
- Consider adding a non-monetary recognition (swag, acknowledgement at all-hands) early — cheaper than paying out time-off.

Appendix: sample MMC tracking columns for sheet (CSV-friendly):
- date, mentor, hire_handle, mmc_amount, activity_type, notes, proof_link, manager_approved (Y/N)

End of draft.

Feedback welcome — ping @sofia in Slack or add notes directly in this doc. Intend to iterate after Sept cohort retro.
